category_title: Students with externalizing behavior problems including work refusal and temper tantrums
scenario_title: Lunchtime 4-square handball session and temper tantrums
minimal_context: The student is participating in a lunchtime 4-square handball game with other students.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Alright, let's start the 4-square handball game. Remember to follow the agreed rules and respectfully take turns while you wait.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm in the square now. I'm going to stay in and beat everyone.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: That ball bounced out of bounds. You are out, so please step out so the next person can play.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: No way! I didn't get out! I'm not going to the back of the line to wait with the other nine kids!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: You have to follow the rules like everyone else. Please step out of the square.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Screams and throws the handball across the playground) It's not fair! I'm not moving and I'm not letting anyone else play!

task.content: Participating in a lunchtime 4-square handball session, requiring turn-taking and rule adherence
task.learning_goal: Following the agreed rules and learning to respectfully take turns

context.social_setting: Up to nine students waiting their turn to get into a square, supervised by the teacher aide and visiting NRL players

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When getting out during the handball game
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Understood what he could actively do to reduce the regulative flares and classroom trouble
related_quotes: if I don’t throw a temper tantrum when I get out, the other kids let me keep playing and want to be my friend

behavior_patterns.condition: When struggling socially with things like that in different environments
